newsitem.title: INDIA: Rising prices keep lid on Indian wheat exports.
newsitem.headline: Rising prices keep lid on Indian wheat exports.

text.p: Rising Indian wheat prices and thin supplies have dampened export demand, traders said on Friday.

"The international demand for Indian wheat is very low as prices have gone up by around $10 (per tonne) in the last fifteen days," said Prem Garg, managing director of Sri Lal Mahal Overseas Ltd in Delhi.
Garg said Indian semi-hard non-durum wheat was currently quoted at around $195 per tonne FOB compared to $185 a fortnight ago.
He said the domestic price of wheat, driven up by thin supplies, had risen 700 rupees to nearly 6,100 rupees per tonne since the start of the season in March.
But prices were expected to fall when the new crop arrives in late February, he said. Traders said this year's wheat crop, aided by plentiful monsoon rains, was progressing well.
"Indian wheat export prices are not in parity with American and Australian wheat," Garg said. American wheat exports were currently priced at between $182 and $183 per tonne, he said.
But Bangladesh and some countries in the Middle East preferred to buy from India due to freight advantage, Garg said.
"Exports to these countries are taking place in small quantities," he said.

Traders said the Agricultural and Processed Foods Products Export Development Authority (APEDA), which handles wheat exports, was yet to issue authorisation certificates to export 1.13 million tonnes of wheat allowed by the government in fiscal 1996/97 (April-March).
"The new quota is still pending," Garg said.
